terra.problem: The line implies that gold from Ophir helped beautify both the temple and Solomon’s palace. The cited verses do not say Ophir’s gold was used in the palace; they say its almug wood was used there.
“Almug wood and gems” includes Solomon’s use of the wood at the LORD’s house and palace, not at Ophir.
“David gives Ophir gold” describes a gift for the temple, not an event at Ophir.
“Jehoshaphat’s ships wrecked” happened at Ezion-geber. The ships never reached Ophir.
Words such as “talents” and “lyres” may need brief explanations for a 5th-grade reader.
